framing_issues.text: County justice leaders and Commissioner Dana Barrett have attacked how the draft is being made.
framing_issues.issue: Loaded verb and unequal verbs. 'Attacked' is stronger than any source verb ('pushing back' P-069, 'objection' P-076, 'alleged' P-072, 'criticized' P-078), while the commission's defender gets 'noted'/'said' (lines 124, 150). Use 'criticized' or 'objected to'.

framing_issues.text: 30-second version: only the critics' objection is summarized
framing_issues.issue: Uneven summary. The overview reports the critics' objection but not the defense in the same sources (Ellis: meetings are open and the full Board votes, P-073/P-079). Add one clause with the defenders' response.

framing_issues.text: The Board must adopt it at its second regular meeting in January.
framing_issues.issue: Misleading timing context. Saying the vote must happen 'at' the January meeting hides that an earlier (December) vote is legal (P-005, P-070), which is exactly the live dispute in Card 5. Readers who rely on the overview could miss an early vote.

framing_issues.text: They sent the Board a letter and said they would skip the commission's budget hearings.
framing_issues.issue: Missing context. P-080 says the justice leaders still submitted their formal 2027 budget requests in writing; the page never says so, so 'skip the hearings' can read as refusing to take part in the budget at all.

framing_issues.text: The county's written instructions say departments' requests could not exceed 5% of their "base budget,"
framing_issues.issue: One side's characterization presented as an official record. The wording is from a WHEREAS clause of Barrett's failed and filed resolution (P-029), but the page attributes it to the county's written instructions, which it says it never found (lines 52, 140, 164).

framing_issues.text: That is about 52 cents of every General Fund dollar.
framing_issues.issue: The arithmetic error makes justice and safety look like a majority of the General Fund. In the neutral overview, that undercuts the justice leaders' underfunding claim. The correct figure is 48 cents (line 187).

framing_issues.text: Savings, called fund balance, cover the gap and rise from $179,000,901 to $252,638,514.
framing_issues.issue: The reversed direction tells readers deficit spending built up reserves. That misstates how much fiscal room there is, which bears directly on Option B's 'Who pays' (added spending needs revenue, cuts or savings).

framing_issues.text: to fix conditions at the Fulton County Jail
framing_issues.issue: Softens the source. The county's own budget book says the agreement was 'to address constitutional violations' at the jail (P-048). Keep the source's words or attribute them.

framing_issues.text: The Board rejected it on Nov 4, by 4 votes to 1.
framing_issues.issue: Procedural mischaracterization with a framing effect. It suggests a merits vote against the cap-removal resolution and recasts the vote to file (P-025) as a rejection. Use 'filed', as lines 109 and 162 do.

framing_issues.text: Vice Chair Abdur-Rahman said, "Those meetings are open meetings."
framing_issues.issue: The misattribution adds a second commission member publicly defending the process. Per P-073 she had not responded, and line 111 says only one commissioner was quoted defending it. This changes the apparent balance of voices.

framing_issues.text: Whether needs are hidden can't be checked until the draft is out.
framing_issues.issue: 'Hidden' implies deliberate concealment and adopts the critics' framing in the page's own voice. Prefer 'whether requests above 5% will appear in the draft'.

framing_issues.text: Solicitor-General Keith Gammage said, "Each year we are underfunded."
framing_issues.issue: Juxtaposition. This general underfunding quote (Atlanta News First, P-071) is placed as support for the 5%-limit claim, although the source does not tie it to the cap.

framing_issues.text: The Board filed the resolution that would have removed it, 4 to 1.
framing_issues.issue: Listed under 'Who disagrees', the filing vote reads as four commissioners disagreeing with the critics on the merits, but the page says no reasons were recorded (lines 105, 111). Note that the vote shows disposition, not stated reasons.

framing_issues.text: Commissioner Ellis said there is no talk of an early vote, Atlanta News First reported.
framing_issues.issue: Placed under 'Who disagrees', but the statement does not dispute waiting until January; if anything it aligns with it. Relabel or move it so readers don't read Ellis as opposing a January vote.

framing_issues.text: "Insufficient staffing and rising caseloads cause backlogs and delays."
framing_issues.issue: The quote is cut before 'in critical probate services' (P-065) and closed with a period, which makes a probate-specific statement read as general.

framing_issues.text: The presentations are the offices' own accounts; our sources have no independent data on caseloads or staffing.
framing_issues.issue: Uneven caveats between sides. Card 6 flags the justice offices' claims as self-reports without independent data, but Card 2 (lines 135-136) gives Ellis's comparative claim ('more transparent and open than anything we've had in recent years') no matching note that it is his own unverified assessment.
